findings.issue: step_commit deletes the fragments from disk (os.remove) BEFORE `git rm`. If `git rm` fails (reproduced on a real scratch git repo with a held .git/index.lock) the step returns False, but the files are already gone from disk while still tracked in HEAD. A resumed step_commit then sees no fragments (read_fragments reads disk), so fragment_findings/assembled_findings return [] and consumed is empty: it commits successfully, and the release commit still carries changelog.d/P9.1.added.md in HEAD (git ls-files changelog.d lists it). The next release assembles that already-released fragment a second time. unconsumed_findings also reads disk only, so verify --release cannot see it.
findings.resolution: Make the deletion one git operation that leaves state intact on failure: run `git rm -q -f --ignore-unmatch -- <fragments>` first (it removes the working file too) and only then os.remove any untracked leftover; or on resume derive `consumed` from `git ls-files changelog.d` as well as the directory. Add a case with a runner whose git rm returns non-zero asserting the files are still on disk and a second step_commit still removes them.

Verified by hand on a scratch git repo seeded with this repository's real CHANGELOG.md: finalize output = the Unreleased text untouched + `### Added/### Fixed` assembled in kind order with P9.2 before P9.10, the old tail byte-identical, length delta exactly the heading rename plus the assembled text; step_commit on a real git index removed the fragments and staged the deletions in the one commit (also with staged-new and staged-modified fragments); a resumed finalize after commit is a no-op. Unknown kind, no kind, empty, own-heading fragments and a hand-edited assembled section are refused (finalize, commit, check), not skipped; wave builder: rl33 one wave vs two. CONTRIBUTING.md states where/kind-less/Unreleased-text-kept/release+verify behaviour; CLAUDE.md states the rule; the product (executor brief, /audit:task add) is named as follow-up, not changed, as asked. The executor's outcome describes the diff accurately, including its own admission that git rm was only exercised against FakeRunner (finding 1 is what a real-git run turned up). Two things the phase description (the stated authority) asks of its first task are neither done nor filed: the PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md list of generatable sections / follow-up, and recording the measured wave width; the task's own acceptance list does not name them, so this is a note for the orchestrator to file as a follow-up, not a divergence. Note also that the 'section matches its fragments' half of the verify --release row is vacuous once the release commit has deleted the fragments (it can only fire between finalize and commit); the real guard there is step_commit.
